          Man Utd Defence Showed Some Fight at Leeds, But Its Makeup Supports Martínez Rant
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
It was nowhere near perfect, but Manchester United's draw at Leeds in the Premier League on Sunday saw them show some fight at the end of a taxing week.
At the end of a long week for Manchester United, a trip to Leeds United and Elland Road was the last thing many would think they needed.
Or maybe it was exactly what their situation required?

Last weekend’s dismal draw with struggling 10-man Tottenham was followed in midweek by a 2-0 defeat at Atlético Madrid. And while the display in Madrid actually wasn’t that bad, the fallout from it plunged United deeper into crisis.
The Argentina defender publicly criticised United’s decision makers in multiple television interviews, most vociferously in an extraordinary exchange on Prime Video.

Among his quotes was this particularly incendiary targeting of United’s technical director, Jason Wilcox: “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”
Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 pic.twitter.com/OGo25Pzd30

The actual content of Martínez’s comments – those above and the rest of the interview – largely resonated with a fanbase who’ve little love for those in charge at the club. But the centre-back was criticised for his timing, with the subsequent circus ultimately a key subject of focus for Carrick in the build-up to the trip to Elland Road, a difficult journey at the best of times.
It was also noted by many that his outburst came during easily his worst run of form personally since joining the club in 2022.

A public apology from Martínez drew a line under the matter, at least officially, and he was named in United’s starting XI on Sunday. Whether that would’ve been the case had the club actually strengthened to the degree he seemingly desired is another matter, but the fact is Carrick didn’t have much choice.

Most have perceived Martínez’s comments to have referenced a lack of investment in defence. After all, the Atlético defeat saw centre-back Ayden Heaven make his Champions League debut at left-back, a position he’d never started a senior game in. He was doing so because Luke Shaw and his deputy, Patrick Dorgu – also not a nominal left-back – were out injured.
And, fittingly, there were more defensive selection issues on Sunday.
Centre-back Leny Yoro started at right-back; right-back Diogo Dalot started at left-back; Martínez was taken off at half-time due to injury.
United finished the game with a back four (going from right to left) of Yoro, Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Dalot; only one of the four was playing in what you’d call their natural position.
As it happened, though, United’s defence deserved praise for the fight they put up in difficult circumstances and against a good, in-form Leeds side. That goes for Martínez, too.

There’ll have been more eyes than usual on him, and having seen Tottenham's Dominic Solanke cause him so much trouble last weekend, it wasn’t surprising to see Leeds target him a couple of times early on with Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
But Martínez made some timely tackles and came out on top in a couple of physical duels. It was a blow to lose him at the break.
Yoro acquitted himself well, not for the first time this term, tucking inside as Leeds lumped numerous crosses in from their right, with the Frenchman clearing nearly all of them.

His eight clearances over the 90 minutes was his second most in a league game for United (second only to tallying 9 vs Leeds in April), and he helped keep Noah Okafor – who scored twice at Old Trafford last term – very quiet.

Dalot, a regular source of frustration among fans, came out with credit, too. Although clearly uncomfortable attacking on his left foot, he showed a willingness to get forward and one of United’s few bright moments in the second half came via solo burst through the middle following a corner.
